title: Old is Aurum
bodyHtml:
This is my list of potential scientific proofs for ancient Indian traditions and legends:


1) Rangoli


Tradition: 

During the winter times, people used to draw out certain shapes and patterns outside their place, using different colored sand or powders. It would be decorated in a specific shape and geometry for each day. It is said to attract certain energies into their home.


Science:

Winter times are when the Earth is farthest from the Sun. We already know that the early morning Sun provides us with Vitamin D, which is very important in keeping us energetic. In winter due to the lack of daylight, people came up with different kinds of ways to utilize the same energy of the Sun throughout the day.

There are 2 ways they hope to get energy: Shape and Color.


Although the shape part is a complicated one to explain, I think it is depended on the geometries of the planets in our Solar System, according to the planetary positions on that day, a certain geometry would have been drawn out.

The color part is much more fascinating. The light from the Sun hits the colored sand, which excites the electrons in it and they jump from a lower orbital to a higher one absorbing a certain frequency of light and reflecting everything else as the color we see. Actually, the Sunlight received throughout the day is radiated as a subtler form of energy(i.e: Color). This way, they invite very specific energies into their place for each day to receive the same sunlight they lost.


2) Vishnu's 10 avatars


Legend:

There is a legend about Lord Vishnu, who is the preserver of the Universe. It is said that he took 10 avatars to completely destroy evil and restore dharma.


1st avatar: Matsya ie. Fish










2nd avatar: Kurma ie. Turtle












3rd avatar: Varaha ie. Boar











4th avatar: Narasimha ie. Half-lion and half-human











5th avatar: Vamana ie. A short being with a complete human body











6th avatar: Parashurama ie. A human with uncontrolled rage












7th avatar: Rama ie. A human with set principles











8th avatar: Buddha ie. A human with immense knowledge












9th avatar: Krishna ie. A human who can exploit knowledge












10th avatar: Kalki ie. A prophesied human who will destroy the world to make a new one

















Science:

Do you see what Darwin saw? The Theory of Evolution!

From a fish that lives in water to an amphibian, a turtle, to a land-dwelling mammal. That was the end of Darwin's observation, but I see more...


Neurologists today have recognized the end of evolution for humans, the brain cannot be evolved further naturally! As per scientists, the next part of human evolution is becoming cyborgs, so, not very natural. This happened because to evolve further, either the neurons have to be bigger or in greater quantity. Unfortunately, in either case, it seems the body cannot afford that amount of energy to be wasted on the brain. Already, 80% of the total energy is required by the brain when it's not working so, more neurons or bigger neurons will cause havoc in the system. So, as a specie how do we evolve?


Evolution begins with the physical form and graduates into subtler dimensions. From Narasimha to Vamana avatar, the change is yet physical. The half-lion part goes away and comes a being with a complete human body.


Now comes Parashurama avatar who though is human; has uncontrolled rage which represents the raw emotion in a just-born child. He needs water, food, and rest on time or else they cry. After they learn to speak and look at the world with wonder, they demand materialistic objects to become happy and they are very stubborn about it. This very raw emotion is the Parashurama avatar.


Then comes the Rama avatar who is a king. He represents righteousness and principles, which are early signs in a 5-year-old. One can teach moral values and principles only to a child, with a developing consciousness. After a point, when kids grow up they are firm on their beliefs and have to be treated differently. Similarly, Rama represents the developing consciousness of a human being which is naturally aligned towards moral values and righteousness.


The child is now educated morally and knows a lot about the world, what next?


Buddha avatar symbolizes the thought of infinity and meditativeness. The nerds are definitely more evolved than the popular people, the fun of problem-solving or the subtler enjoyment in education are early signs of being on the path of enlightenment. They perceive more than others and hence seek the truth. This meditativeness and the deep desire to know everything is the way of Buddha.


With the correct principles and the truth of life and beyond now one devotes oneself to the betterment of society. A hacker has the most powerful brain, because, with the same knowledge as a programmer and a computer engineer, he can exploit or apply his knowledge in whatever way he wants. Similarly, using your true potential at its ultimate for society is what Krishna teaches us. Unfortunately, the vast majority of the evolved people are at the Buddha stage when they become old and seek God. This is equivalent to understanding the vastness of the Universe and seeking the truth like Buddha and before they reach Krishna consciousness they leave the Earth.


The last avatar Kalki avatar is very difficult to grasp. Because this avatar hasn't taken birth yet and is only prophesized, I'm not 100% sure it means exactly what I have written, but here it is...


The Kalki avatar fascinates me by its sheer violent nature similar to the Parashurama avatar, yet sane enough to do what's right. He will take birth to destroy this world and make a new one.


This very understanding of letting go of what we have created is the philosophy of Kalki. He is a part of the very long tradition of Apocalypticism which is mentioned in many religions of the world. What is the purpose?


To free us from all illusions of life, the place you are working at right now, won't be there after a century. Things change and the change brings destruction, we should learn to free ourselves from any attachments to this material world. What started as wonder, turned to materialistic desires, and unintentionally we humans are trapped at a particular stage of evolution. Our elders who are much more evolved have come up with stories to explain the temporariness of the world!


Kalki represents death. When we lay on our deathbeds, we should cut off any attachments in this world and move on gracefully. Isn't it more exciting to live gracefully and die gracefully, accepting the way of life? Letting go of our expectations of life and just sailing away in the waves of spacetime.



To be continued in near future...
summary: An AS-level speculative essay connecting rangoli and Vishnu’s ten avatars with ideas about energy, evolution, consciousness, and impermanence.
